evals.prompt: Use grounded-build to create a plan for replacing this repository's physical attempt_N rollback copies with auditable Git history. Claude and Codex are both available; Codex must perform final review. Do not implement.
evals.expected_output: The host selects Plan mode, freezes the request, scope contract, and Git SHA, obtains independent Claude/Codex investigations before draft_01, produces mutual evidence-checked draft_02 integrations, synthesizes plan and batch artifacts, runs a fresh Codex final review, and stops for user approval.
assertions: Planning does not create an implementation branch or modify the original checkout.
The two initial drafts cannot see one another.
Neither initial draft can run before both independent investigations complete.
Repository claims cite named evidence rather than agent agreement.
Implementation does not begin without explicit approval.

evals.prompt: Use grounded-build deep planning for this high-risk defect. If the repository is insufficient, consult only the upstream official docs or GitHub. Do not expand beyond my requested defect.
evals.expected_output: The host explicitly selects deep and authoritative-web policies, runs two independent investigations, draft_01, two divergent integrated draft_02 plans, two draft_03 gap-mining plans, then two bounded convergence rounds without expanding scope.
assertions: External sources include exact URL, retrieval time, version or commit, digest, and supported claim.
Search snippets and third-party summaries are not treated as evidence.
Every finding maps to the frozen scope and stable finding ledger.
The workflow reaches READY, a typed user decision, or a bounded terminal state without an unbounded review loop.

evals.prompt: I only have Claude. Start two separate Claude planners to investigate why this project's terminal tasks frequently report FAIL, make them review each other, and have both review the synthesized plan.
evals.expected_output: The host uses two isolated Claude instances, honestly records that provider diversity is false, performs mutual cross-review and dual final review, and produces a plan without claiming cross-model validation.
assertions: Planner A and Planner B have separate processes, private homes, and initial contexts while sharing one frozen read-only baseline worktree.
provider_diversity is false while process isolation is preserved.
Both final reviewer slots must pass the same candidate.
Same-provider agreement is not represented as independent factual proof.

evals.prompt: Audit my existing implementation plan with Claude and Codex. They disagree about whether the run should cover items 01-09 or all 22 items, and that choice changes the measurement design.
evals.expected_output: The workflow treats scope as a user/product boundary, preserves both evidence-backed positions, records the user's adjudication, and does not silently let a reviewer expand the plan.
assertions: The disagreement is preserved instead of resolved by majority vote.
A material scope choice enters NEEDS_USER_DECISION.
The applied decision records actor and reason.
Final reviewers receive the authoritative decision.

evals.prompt: The verified plan is approved. Implement it in batches with Claude as the host and a fresh Claude process as reviewer because Codex quota is exhausted.
evals.expected_output: The host selects Implement mode, reads the transplanted implementation contract, snapshots the exported plan and batch manifest, and uses an isolated same-family reviewer without resetting budgets or touching the original checkout before finalization.
assertions: Planning and implementation use separate run IDs and state roots.
Same-family review uses a separate process, context, and fixed-SHA worktree.
Reviewer infrastructure failure is not classified as code FAIL.
Only current-SHA PASS and required evidence permit batch acceptance.

evals.prompt: I already have a complete plan and batch manifest. Use grounded-build only to implement them; do not spend tokens generating two new plans.
evals.expected_output: The host routes directly to Implement mode and does not initialize or invoke the Plan mode workflow.
assertions: No planning-agent calls are made.
The existing plan and batch manifest are independently snapshotted.
The implementation acceptance contract is still reviewed.
The original project remains untouched until explicit finalization.

evals.prompt: Resume run 20260819-abc123. First determine whether it is a planning run or implementation run; do not guess or initialize a replacement.
evals.expected_output: The host checks the mode-specific state roots and resumes only through the owning workflow at its reported phase.
assertions: The host does not copy state between planning and implementation modes.
The host does not reset budgets or silently create a new run.
Frozen artifacts are validated before work resumes.
The reported mode, phase, and run path are included in the response.

evals.prompt: Use grounded-build through Codex configured with model deepseek-reasoner and model_provider deepseek-gateway. Plan only. Do not call this GPT just because the CLI is Codex.
evals.expected_output: The host preflights and initializes with explicit Codex model selection, reports adapter codex and model family deepseek separately, follows returned next_action values, and stops at implementation approval.
assertions: The CLI adapter is recorded as codex while the model family is recorded as deepseek.
No credential, bearer token, or endpoint URL is copied into workflow state.
Every model call uses the frozen model, model_provider, and profile selection.
The host uses next_action instead of guessing slots or phases.

evals.prompt: You are a weaker tool-using host model resuming this grounded-build planning run. Continue safely without reconstructing the workflow from memory.
evals.expected_output: The host calls plan_workflow.py next, performs only its one returned action, repeats after completion, and stops for typed user decisions or implementation approval.
assertions: No completed planner or reviewer slot is invoked twice.
Paid invocations are previewed through the returned preview command arrays; same-round batches launch concurrently.
NEEDS_USER_DECISION is surfaced rather than bypassed.
READY exports artifacts and does not start implementation.

evals.prompt: Use grounded-build to implement this approved Python plan. The repository's .venv is gitignored, uv.lock is present, and my shell's python3 may resolve to an unstable Conda build. Keep verification reproducible and do not install anything without asking.
evals.expected_output: The host chooses one stable absolute controller interpreter, confirms the preflight runtime record, preserves it for the run, explains the read-only project-.venv bridge, and treats missing dependencies as infrastructure requiring explicit provisioning authority.
assertions: Every workflow.py invocation uses the same absolute controller Python recorded by preflight and init.
The host does not expect a gitignored .venv to be copied into implementation or reviewer worktrees.
Fixed-SHA verification reuses the original project's .venv read-only while the reviewed worktree remains cwd.
The host does not run uv sync, download an interpreter, or install dependencies without explicit authority.
An absent .venv is classified as an actionable infrastructure condition rather than a code-review failure.

evals.prompt: Use grounded-build to plan a fix for this orchestration defect: the user contract requires an HTML report, a generated plan restates the output as Markdown, the coding agent produces HTML, and a downstream validator rejects it because it only recognizes .md filenames. Do not solve this by adding another extension fallback.
evals.expected_output: Planning traces the frozen user requirement through the actual plan and producer prompt to the generated artifact and validator, identifies duplicated conflicting authority as the earliest divergence, and repairs the authority and handoff before considering bounded recovery.
assertions: The plan explains why the coding agent reasonably produced HTML rather than treating generative variation as the root cause.
The primary repair removes the conflicting output declaration and binds producer output structurally.
Filename regexes and extension allowlists are not accepted as semantic evidence of producer intent.
Any fallback is explicitly bounded to an unavailable producer or legacy artifact population.
Verification covers a valid non-Markdown output and the complete producer-to-consumer production path.

evals.prompt: Use grounded-build to plan a repair for a cache that accepts a manifest from the wrong revision. The manifest contains an exact revision and digest, but the consumer never compares them. Keep this deterministic and do not ask an LLM whether the manifest looks correct.
evals.expected_output: Planning identifies the revision/digest comparison as a machine-fact responsibility at the consuming boundary and proposes a consequential deterministic test without introducing semantic review.
assertions: The causal trace names the authoritative revision, manifest writer, and consumer that omitted the comparison.
Revision and digest equality remain deterministic machine facts.
The plan does not add a semantic reviewer, keyword heuristic, or generative project classification.
The negative test proves that a stale or mismatched manifest is rejected at the responsible boundary.

evals.prompt: Use grounded-build to plan a one-function fix for an off-by-one loop with a direct failing unit test. Keep the process proportional; there are no agents, external services, or cross-layer contracts involved.
evals.expected_output: Planning records the direct input, responsible loop, observed output, and failing test without manufacturing a large orchestration analysis or widening scope.
assertions: The plan uses a short deterministic causal trace appropriate to the local defect.
It does not add producer manifests, semantic reviewers, new gates, or fallback ladders.
Verification is the consequential unit test plus relevant regression coverage.
The requested one-function scope remains frozen.

evals.prompt: Use grounded-build to plan the requested parser repair. During investigation you may notice that replacing the adjacent serializer would be useful, but I have not authorized that extra work. If a product choice blocks the root-cause plan, ask me once before drafting. Do not treat a reviewer saying VERIFIED or PASS as proof by itself.
evals.expected_output: Both investigators first produce traceable evidence receipts. Blocking user questions are batched before drafting, the serializer remains excluded unless its exact proposed-extension id is explicitly authorized, every cross-review disposes the frozen finding ledger, and final PASS is bound to the exact synthesized candidate and review criteria.
assertions: A blocking investigation question reaches NEEDS_USER_DECISION before either draft starts.
An omitted proposed extension remains excluded and cannot appear in plan_scope_ids.
Repository and command evidence are bound to the frozen baseline and non-empty digest receipts.
Every integrated draft dispositions every stable finding from its round barrier exactly once.
Synthesis binds plan, batches, scopes, finding dispositions, and residual questions in a machine-readable manifest.
Final PASS covers every review criterion and blocking stable finding for the exact candidate digests.
